taxonomy.healthy: Motor operating without the listed faults.
taxonomy.rotor_unbalance: An uneven distribution of mass about the rotor axis.
taxonomy.rotor_misalignment: Misalignment between the motor shaft and the coupled shaft.
taxonomy.stator_winding: An electrical fault in the stator winding.
taxonomy.voltage_unbalance: Unbalanced supply voltages across the motor phases.
taxonomy.broken_rotor_bars: Broken conductor bars in the rotor.

direct-v1.instructions: Listen to this ten-second industrial motor recording. Select the single most plausible provisional condition from the supplied taxonomy using audible evidence. Account for changing speed, load, background noise and overlapping signatures. Ground the selection in this recording. Healthy requires positive supporting evidence. Return null when the audible evidence leaves plausible categories unresolved. Report a self-assessed score between zero and one, with uncalibrated uncertainty.
direct-v1.response_contract: Return one JSON object with exactly three fields: label (one taxonomy key or null), score (a finite number from 0 to 1), and observations (an array of brief descriptions of directly audible features).

evidence-v1.instructions: Analyze the supplied ten-second motor audio. Identify directly audible tones, broadband noise, impacts, periodic amplitude changes, roughness and time evolution. Cite numerical quantities only when supplied as measurements. Assess these features jointly against the taxonomy: periodicity can accompany imbalance, misalignment or a bent shaft; hum can have several electrical and operational causes. Account for speed and load changes. Choose a category when positive audible evidence favors it over the alternatives; otherwise return null. Healthy also requires supporting evidence. Use general engineering knowledge together with the supplied recording. The score is an uncalibrated self-assessment. Keep observations grounded in audible evidence.
